gaps.sentence: Your luggage ___ (weigh) at check-in, so allow extra time.
gaps.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + weighed. The agent (staff) is obvious.

gaps.sentence: A cheaper version of the vaccine ___ right now.
gaps.explanation: 'Right now' requires present continuous passive: is being + developed.

gaps.sentence: The ambush ___ (plan) by someone with intimate knowledge of the valley.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive (had been planned) stresses completion before the ambush; was planned is also acceptable.

gaps.sentence: I must get my passport ___ (renew) before the trip.
gaps.explanation: 'Get + object + past participle': the passport is renewed by an authority, not by me.

gaps.sentence: The refugees ___ (provide) with blankets and hot meals last night.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: were + provided. Note the pattern provide somebody WITH something.

gaps.sentence: The house looked deserted; it ___ (empty) years earlier.
gaps.hint: past event before another past point
gaps.explanation: 'Years earlier' is before the past reference point, so past perfect passive: had been + emptied.

gaps.sentence: He refuses ___ (tell) what to do by people he's never met.
gaps.explanation: 'Refuse' takes a to-infinitive; passive meaning needs to be + told.

gaps.sentence: The castle ___ (restore) at present, so the east wing is closed to visitors.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + restored for work in progress now.
